GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg.notes: brace-expansion DoS via unbounded expansion length (OOM crash). NOT REACHABLE from the shipped app: brace-expansion is never imported by electron/, src/ or packages/, and never appears in the vite-built main or renderer bundles. audit-ci reports 20 advisory paths (8 physical copies in node_modules), every one of them under lint/build/CI tooling — eslint 8 (direct minimatch ^3.1.2 plus @eslint/eslintrc, file-entry-cache), @typescript-eslint 7, the electron-builder packaging chain (@electron/asar, dir-compare, ejs>jake>filelist, electron-winstaller), @sentry/vite-plugin, test-exclude, and the npm vendored inside @semantic-release/npm. Exploitation needs an attacker-controlled glob pattern; every glob pattern on these paths comes from our own repo config, never from email or network input. NOT FIXABLE BY A BUMP OR AN OVERRIDE: upstream patched only 5.0.8 and backported nothing to the 1.x/2.x lines (1.1.16 and 2.1.2 are newest in their lines and both sit inside the vulnerable <=5.0.7 range), while 5.x changed the CommonJS export shape from `module.exports = expand` to `exports.expand`, so a blanket `overrides` to 5.0.8 breaks the brace-expansion code paths of minimatch 3.x/9.x consumers (minimatch 9.0.9 calls `brace_expansion_1.default(pattern)`, minimatch 3.1.5 calls the module object directly). A compatible fork or patch-package shim would avoid that break but carries its own maintenance burden, so this is 'no safe drop-in fix', not 'physically impossible'. Upgrading to eslint 9 does NOT clear it: verified 2026-07-25 that eslint 9.39.5 still declares minimatch ^3.1.5 directly and still depends on @eslint/eslintrc ^3.3.6 (itself minimatch ^3.1.5). The eslint chain only clears at eslint 10, which dropped @eslint/eslintrc and moved to minimatch ^10 as of 10.0.0 (10.8.0 is at ^10.2.5) — so the target is 10.x, not any 10.8+ specifically. So the eslint chain needs a two-major jump (8.57.1 -> 10.x, flat-config migration) plus @typescript-eslint 8+, and even after that the electron-builder-internal chains and the vendored npm stay outside our control. Re-triage when the eslint 10 migration lands, when electron-builder's own tree moves off minimatch 3.x, or when upstream backports a patch to the 1.x/2.x lines. SCOPE TRADE-OFF (deliberate, flagged LOW by codex-security-review 2026-07-25): this entry allowlists the bare advisory id, so it also suppresses the advisory on any FUTURE path, including a runtime one. audit-ci path-scoping (`ADVISORY|root>...`) was measured as the alternative and rejected: the advisory currently spans 20 distinct dependency roots, so path-scoping means 20 near-duplicate entries, and it turns every benign new tooling root into a red pipeline while still not distinguishing 'new dev tooling' from the case that actually matters ('brace-expansion is now in the shipped bundle'). The precise guard for that case is a bundle-level check, tracked as §2.57.f1; until it exists, the 2026-10-01 expiry is the backstop that forces a re-look.
